title: Prop-Firm Risk vs Personal Capital
hook: The chart can be the same. The account decision can be different.

launchpad.outcome: Size the account, not just the chart, and write your own risk framework.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Does this trade fit THIS account?

slides.heading: Two kinds of account

beats.title: Personal account
beats.line: Available capital, your risk tolerance, broker margin, your rules.

beats.title: Prop / evaluation
beats.line: Also: max drawdown, daily loss rules, trailing drawdown, consistency, contract limits, payout and time rules.

slides.punch: CHECK CURRENT RULES FOR THE ACTUAL PROGRAM YOU TRADE. Firms change them.

slides.title: Same PIL, same ICC, same 30-point stop

asks.prompt: Same contract size in both, automatically?

options.label: Yes, same chart
options.feedback: Account B would lose most of its remaining drawdown on one full loss.

options.label: No
options.why: The account decides the size. Account B needs a smaller size, or no trade.

slides.punch: THE CHART CAN BE THE SAME. THE ACCOUNT DECISION CAN BE DIFFERENT.

slides.quote: The chart can be the same. The account decision can be different.

slides.prompt: What does protecting your account mean beyond using a stop?
slides.modelAnswer: Sizing from my risk cap, respecting a daily limit and a maximum number of trades, keeping room for losing streaks, and checking the real constraints of the account I’m trading.

takeaways: Size the account, not the chart.
remember: The chart can be the same. The account decision can be different.
